target.title: fix(qa): restore automatic smoke coverage across channels
target.body:
Related: #101164
Related: #101184
Supersedes: #101187

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where automatic QA Smoke CI selected one shared multi-channel profile, causing the suite resolver to reject the run before any channel scenario could execute.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workflow now plans three deterministic channel-compatible shards from the current smoke profile: one Matrix shard and two balanced Telegram shards. Each shard runs independently while one aggregate required status stays fail-closed. Slack and WhatsApp restart/resume scenarios require their live channel drivers because Crabline does not satisfy those inbound/auth contracts; the silence-sensitive Telegram baseline is isolated from concurrent transport traffic.

## User Impact

Maintainers regain reliable automatic Matrix and Telegram smoke coverage without weakening the shared profile's cross-channel taxonomy. Slack and WhatsApp restart/resume coverage remains in the live-driver lanes instead of failing the simulated automatic lane.

## Evidence

- Exact CI on the original sharding patch proved Matrix and one Telegram shard, then exposed the repaired contracts: unsupported simulated Slack/WhatsApp restart paths and concurrent Telegram traffic contaminating a silence assertion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28820059322
- Focused planner, scenario-catalog, and workflow-guard coverage: 70 tests passed; 89 scenarios are selected exactly once across three shards.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml`, `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs`, targeted `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview on the complete replacement diff: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.
- Blacksmith Testbox remained queued and direct AWS warmup was interrupted by a coordinator code restart; exact-head hosted CI remains the merge authority.
- This PR replaces #101164, which GitHub would not reopen after its source branch was force-updated. It targets current `main` after #101184 reverted the temporary single-channel workaround.
